meta.description: Credited to Margaret Thatcher for decades — but no speech, interview or book has ever been named. The trail stops at a 1989 quotation dictionary.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'You may have to fight a battle more than once to win it'?
meta.ogDescription: Thatcher said something close in 1984. This tidier, more quotable version has never been traced to anything she actually delivered.

answer.label: Attributed to Margaret Thatcher
answer.sourceLine: No primary source has ever been produced for this sentence. It is not in Wikiquote’s sourced Thatcher material; it sits in the Disputed section ↗, where the editors note it is “widely attributed to Margaret Thatcher on various websites, and also appears in a number of books” — but “without any further source information such as date, location or any other context.” The oldest appearance they can name is a 1989 quotation dictionary. Thatcher did say something close in 1984, and that line is sourced; this one is not.

source.excerpt: You may have to fight a battle more than once to win it.
trail: Checked Quote Investigator’s Margaret Thatcher archive ↗ first. QI has investigated four Thatcher-linked sayings; this is not one of them, so there is no specialist verdict to defer to.

Read the raw wikitext of the Wikiquote Margaret Thatcher page ↗. The line appears only in the Disputed section, with the editors’ note that it circulates “without any further source information such as date, location or any other context.”

Confirmed the reference book exists and matches the citation: The Concise Columbia Dictionary of Quotations ↗, Robert Andrews, Columbia University Press, 1989, ISBN 0231069901, viii + 343 pages — so a page 320 is real. The scan is lending-restricted, so the page itself could not be read here; the page number comes from Wikiquote.

Noted the documented near-miss. Wikiquote transcribes Thatcher’s Second Carlton Lecture (26 November 1984) as “may have to fight fundamental battles anew,” and a 2003 Atlantic Bridge speech as “every generation has to fight anew the battle for liberty.” Both are sourced to the Margaret Thatcher Foundation archive, which is not reachable from this run — the wording above is Wikiquote’s transcription, not a reading of the original.
source.excerptNote: There is no fuller context to show, and that is the finding. What Thatcher is documented as saying is a rougher, less aphoristic version of the same thought — Wikiquote transcribes this from her Second Carlton Lecture of 26 November 1984: “each generation has to stand up for democracy. It can’t take anything for granted and may have to fight fundamental battles anew.” The polished sentence people quote is not that sentence.
source.rightsNote: No rights status is asserted, because no source work has been established. If the sentence originates in a Thatcher speech, that speech is in copyright; if it is a later compiler’s condensation, the compiler’s wording is in copyright too. Either way it is not public domain, and nothing here should be read as clearing it for reuse.

author.name: Margaret Thatcher
author.heading: About Margaret Thatcher
author.bio: Margaret Thatcher was Britain’s first woman Prime Minister and its longest-serving of the twentieth century, in office from 1979 to 1990. She was an unusually quotable politician, and an unusually well-archived one: the Margaret Thatcher Foundation holds transcripts of her speeches and interviews going back to the 1940s. That archive is the reason a Thatcher line with no traceable occasion stands out. The words that survive best in circulation are often not the words she used — they are the tidied-up version someone else wrote later.

misattribution.heading: Why this one keeps getting a source it does not have
misattribution.intro: Nobody appears to have invented this line maliciously. It reads like Thatcher, it compresses a thought she genuinely held, and it has been passed between reference books and quote sites for thirty-five years without anyone attaching an occasion to it.

items.why: The Wikiquote Thatcher page ↗ places it under Disputed and states plainly that it circulates “without any further source information such as date, location or any other context.”

Wikiquote transcribes her as saying democracy “can’t take anything for granted and may have to fight fundamental battles anew” on 26 November 1984. Same idea, rougher phrasing, and it is sourced — unlike the version in circulation.

items.who: The Concise Columbia Dictionary of Quotations, 1989
items.why: A quotation dictionary is a place where sayings get recorded, not where they get documented. The 1989 volume ↗ is real and the page is real, but per Wikiquote the entry carries no occasion.

misattribution.truthLine: The honest answer is that this is probably Thatcher and certainly unproven. If you need a Thatcher line on persistence that you can actually cite, use the sourced 1984 one ↗ instead.

context.heading: The gap between what she said and what we quote
lead: Thatcher is one of the best-documented politicians in British history. The Margaret Thatcher Foundation has published transcripts of her speeches, interviews and press conferences across five decades, and researchers routinely pin her remarks to a specific room on a specific afternoon. Against that background, a famous Thatcher sentence with no occasion attached is genuinely odd.

The likeliest explanation is not fabrication but polish. Spoken political rhetoric is baggy; the sentences that survive in circulation are usually shorter and neater than anything actually delivered. Somewhere between a lectern in 1984 and a quotation dictionary in 1989, a rough clause about fighting fundamental battles anew became a clean, symmetrical aphorism — and the clean version is the one that travelled.
context.detailsSummary: What we could and could not check
detailsBody: The Margaret Thatcher Foundation’s own archive is blocked by this run’s network policy, so every wording of hers quoted on this page comes from Wikiquote’s transcription rather than from the original transcript. That is a real limitation and it is stated rather than hidden.

The 1989 Columbia dictionary was confirmed to exist with the editor, publisher, year, ISBN and length Wikiquote gives, which makes the page-320 citation plausible. The scan is lending-restricted, so the entry itself was not read here.
context.pull: A famous Thatcher line with no occasion attached is odd — her archive is one of the most complete in British politics.

Robert Andrews, p. 320, but without any further source information such as date, location or context; it also gives the 1984 Second Carlton Lecture line "may have to fight fundamental battles anew" as a possible basis.

The Concise Columbia Dictionary of Quotations by Robert Andrews was published by Columbia University Press, New York, in 1989, ISBN 0231069901, viii+343 pages; the scan is access-restricted (lending only).
Quote Investigator's Margaret Thatcher category lists four investigated Thatcher-linked quotations and does not include this line.
